title.en: The Danny Casey story and the lonely wait

hook.en: Have you ever told a story so many times that you half believed it yourself? Sophie claims she has met a famous young footballer, and then she waits for him to come back.

objectives.en: Trace the sequence of events in the story
Interpret the ending at the lonely meeting place

narration.en: Have you ever told a story so many times that you half believed it yourself? Sophie claims she has met a famous young footballer, and then she waits for him to come back.

body.en: Sophie tells Geoff that she has met Danny Casey, a young Irish football star who plays for United. She says he spoke to her and promised to meet her again, but she has no proof, not even an autograph. Geoff doubts her, and her father dismisses the story as another of her fantasies.

points.en: Danny Casey: young Irish football star of United
Sophie claims a chance meeting with him
No proof: not even an autograph

steps.en: Sophie tells Geoff she has met Danny Casey
She says he promised to meet her again
She has no proof, not even an autograph
Geoff doubts her and her father dismisses the story
She goes alone to a quiet spot to wait
She imagines every detail of the meeting
Slowly she realises he is not coming
Sad, she worries most about what to tell others

explanation.en: The wait shows how far her fantasy has run ahead of her real life.

body.en: Sophie goes alone to a quiet spot to wait for Danny Casey, imagining every detail of the meeting. As time passes, she realises he is not coming, and she feels a deep sadness. Yet she does not fully give up the dream; she worries most about what she will tell others.

problem.en: Do you think Sophie really met Danny Casey? Give reasons from the story.

steps.en: Point out the lack of proof: no autograph and no witness.
Recall her habit of daydreaming and her father's and Geoff's doubts.
Use the ending: Casey never turns up for the promised meeting.
Conclude that the meeting was most likely a fantasy born of hero-worship.

answer.en: Most likely not. Sophie had no proof, her family knew her as a dreamer, and Casey never came to the meeting. The encounter seems to be a fantasy created by her admiration for a star and her longing to escape her dull life.
